boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Quinnipiac settings for solo focus, collaborative work and between-class study across Mount Carmel and North Haven.

cards.title: Arnold Bernhard Library
cards.subtitle: Mount Carmel Campus
cards.notes: Choose a whiteboard room, lounge chair or computer table based on the task, then reserve a study room in MyQ if your group needs one.
cards.short_summary: A library setting with several documented seating and study-room formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac identifies whiteboard rooms, comfortable chairs and computer tables among the study options in Arnold Bernhard Library.
cards.source_title: Top study spaces around our campuses heading into midterms week
cards.access_notes: The 2025–26 undergraduate catalog lists regular-semester building hours; check MyQ for updates and reserve rooms ahead when needed.

cards.title: Edward and Barbara Netter Library
cards.subtitle: Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences Building, North Haven Campus
cards.notes: Use the window-side chairs and ottomans for individual reading, and confirm your campus access before making the trip to North Haven.
cards.short_summary: A health-sciences library with window seating and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Edward and Barbara Netter Library has comfortable chairs and ottomans by windows and is open to the Quinnipiac community.
cards.access_notes: Currently open only to the Quinnipiac University community; the university lists regular hours and advises contacting the library for updates.

cards.title: Lynne L. Pantalena Law Library
cards.subtitle: School of Law Center, North Haven Campus
cards.notes: Use a reading area for quiet work or the Library Commons for collaborative work, while observing the access rules for the law-school community.
cards.short_summary: A three-story law library with reading rooms, collaborative space and a Library Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lynne L. Pantalena Law Library includes collaborative-work space, reading rooms and the Library Commons for law students and professional groups.
cards.access_notes: Currently open only to the Quinnipiac University community; its page identifies the Library Commons as dedicated to law students and professional groups.

cards.entity_name: Communications, Computing and Engineering Study Area
cards.title: Communications, Computing and Engineering
cards.subtitle: Mount Carmel Campus
cards.notes: Set up in the renovated building’s couch or whiteboard-room areas, and avoid entering maker spaces, classrooms or labs that are not open to you.
cards.short_summary: A renovated academic-building study area with couches and whiteboard rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac describes study areas in the Communications, Computing and Engineering building with couches, whiteboard rooms and proximity to the Innovation Hub MakerSpace.
cards.source_title: Top study spaces around our campuses heading into midterms week
cards.access_notes: Use publicly open study areas only; classrooms, labs and maker spaces may have separate access or scheduling requirements.

cards.entity_name: School of Computing and Engineering Basement Study Space
cards.title: School of Computing and Engineering Basement Study Space
cards.subtitle: Basement of the Communications, Computing and Engineering Building
cards.notes: Head to the basement when you want a quieter library-like setting, and follow posted directions for any adjacent academic or technical spaces.
cards.short_summary: A documented quiet study location in the CCE building basement.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac identifies a quiet, library-like study spot in the basement of the Communications, Computing and Engineering building.
cards.source_title: Top study spaces around our campuses heading into midterms week
cards.access_notes: Use only areas open to students at the time of your visit; nearby classrooms and technical facilities may be restricted.

cards.title: School of Business Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Mount Carmel Campus
cards.notes: Use the tables near the building entrance for project work, and yield the area if it is assigned for a class, meeting or university event.
cards.short_summary: Bright entry-area tables suited to collaborative coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac describes the School of Business as having well-lit study areas near its entrance, with tables and spaces for group work.
cards.source_title: Top study spaces around our campuses heading into midterms week
cards.access_notes: Common-area availability can change with classes and events; use only seating that is open at the time of your visit.

cards.entity_name: Center for Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences Second-Floor Study Space
cards.title: Center for Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences — Second Floor
cards.subtitle: North Haven Campus
cards.notes: Go upstairs from the dining hall for a naturally lit quiet-work setting, and confirm access to the North Haven academic building before arrival.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor quiet area with ample natural light above the dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac identifies a quiet study space with ample natural light on the second floor of the Center for Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences, above the dining hall.
cards.source_title: Top study spaces around our campuses heading into midterms week
cards.access_notes: Located on the North Haven Campus; use only publicly available seating and follow building access guidance.

cards.title: The SITE Lobby
cards.subtitle: Science, Innovation, Technology and Exploration Building, South Quad
cards.notes: Use the lobby seating for a short independent block or informal collaboration, keeping circulation routes clear and respecting scheduled building activity.
cards.short_summary: A central gathering space with seating in Quinnipiac’s newest South Quad academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac states that the lobby of The SITE is a central gathering space designed to encourage collaboration and connection.
cards.access_notes: The SITE contains academic and event facilities; use open lobby seating and follow any event, class or building-access directions.

cards.title: The SITE Third-Floor Lounge Areas
cards.subtitle: Science, Innovation, Technology and Exploration Building, South Quad
cards.notes: Bring a laptop and headphones for focused work between classes, and share lounge seating with others using the academic building.
cards.short_summary: Third-floor lounges designed for collaboration, informal meetings and focused study.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac says students use third-floor lounge areas in The SITE for collaboration, informal meetings and focused study between classes.
cards.access_notes: Access and seating availability can be affected by classes and events; use available common areas only.

cards.entity_name: The SITE Second-Floor Flexible Study and Collaboration Spaces
cards.title: The SITE Second-Floor Flexible Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Science, Innovation, Technology and Exploration Building, South Quad
cards.notes: Use these flexible areas for discussion or team planning, and relocate if a scheduled class, meeting or university activity needs the space.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor spaces intended to support discussion, teamwork and peer learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Quinnipiac describes flexible study and collaboration spaces on the second floor of The SITE as encouraging discussion, teamwork and peer learning.
cards.access_notes: Use only areas open at the time of your visit; academic spaces may be affected by class and event schedules.

warnings: North Haven Campus locations are part of Quinnipiac University but are outside Hamden.
Confirm current building access and room availability before visiting; only the university community currently has access to the Netter and Pantalena libraries.
